answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require proof of sustained useful work before granting voting weight: each identity earns reputation only by completing verified tasks over time, like a copper coin slowly minted through real service rather than bought in bulk. A newcomer starts as an isolated island with no influence, and trust grows gradually — a lotus rising through repeated honest attestations from distinct, established peers. Creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing, because each must independently pay the same time and work cost before its vote counts.
